ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Lorraine Hansberry — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Diagnosis of pancreatic adenocarcinoma: tumor board plan, medical oncology consultation, genetic counseling, early palliative care, and planning of chemotherapy before surgery

text.paragraph: Diagnosis visit: biopsy results, the tumor board plan, and the oncology consultation. [S]

Ms. Hansberry returns two weeks after her first visit. Upper endoscopy two days after that visit found no ulcer but an ulcerated mass in the duodenum next to the papilla, oozing slowly, and the biopsies show adenocarcinoma. The pancreas-protocol CT the next day showed a 3.1 cm mass in the head of the pancreas invading the duodenum, with dilated bile and pancreatic ducts and contact with more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, but no contact with the arteries and no spread to the liver, peritoneum or lungs. Endoscopic ultrasound a week ago confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma on biopsy, and a metal stent was placed in the bile duct at the same session; her urine is lighter and the itching has gone. The tumor board reviewed her five days ago. She had two doses of intravenous iron and has had no more black stools. Pain in the upper abdomen and back is 6 out of 10 and wakes her. Her stools are pale and float after fatty meals. She saw Dr. Adeyemi-Rourke this morning and genetic counseling this afternoon. She asked to be told everything plainly and was. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 1963-05-04; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Thin, tired, composed; weight 55.4 kg; blood pressure 108/68, pulse 92
Slight scleral icterus, less than at the first visit
Tender in the epigastrium without guarding; no mass felt; no liver enlargement; no ascites
No supraclavicular nodes; no umbilical nodule
No calf tenderness or leg swelling
Direct, asks exact questions, writes down the answers; tearful briefly

Epigastric pain for about two months, boring through to the back and worse after meals and lying flat, with nausea, early fullness, a loss of 5 kg (8 percent of her weight), and pale, loose stools: an upper abdominal cause such as a bleeding ulcer or a pancreatic or duodenal tumor must be found. Upper endoscopy and pancreas-protocol CT booked this week
S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented collapse in pain and the account of a suspected duodenal ulcer. Superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Iron deficiency anemia from chronic upper gastrointestinal blood loss: black stools on and off for three weeks, two near-fainting spells, hemoglobin 9.1 g/dL, MCV 74 fL, ferritin 6 ng/mL
S — Synthetic finding anchored to the documented account that she was told she had anemia and bleeding ulcers.

New hyperglycemia: A1c 6.6% and random glucose 132 mg/dL in a lean woman of 32 who is losing weight; new diabetes with weight loss can be the first sign of a pancreatic cancer, so it is to be confirmed and explained, not labeled type 2
S — Synthetic finding; superseded when diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer was recorded at the second visit.

Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, 3.1 cm, invading the duodenum, borderline resectable (tumor contact of more than half the circumference of the superior mesenteric vein, no arterial contact), no distant spread, CA 19-9 486 U/mL after biliary drainage; on EUS-guided biopsy; synthetic modern detail linked to her documented cancer, whose primary site the sources record differently
S — Synthetic histology, site, stage and course; the sources say she died of cancer and differ on whether it was pancreatic, duodenal, or colonic with spread to the pancreas (R). See sources.md.

S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor.

S — Synthetic consequence of the synthetic tumor; diagnosed clinically, as guidance allows in pancreatic cancer.
Cancer-related pain in the upper abdomen and back, 6 out of 10, with sleep broken by it
S — Synthetic symptom of the synthetic tumor.

list.item:
Adenocarcinoma of the head of the pancreas, borderline resectable (C25.0). Pancreatic adenocarcinoma diagnosed two weeks after she first came, because the pain with weight loss, the anemia and the new diabetes were investigated at once rather than put down to stress. It is borderline resectable because of the venous contact, with no arterial involvement and no distant spread. The tumor board and Dr. Adeyemi-Rourke recommend modified FOLFIRINOX before surgery, which she is fit for (ECOG 1, normal kidney and liver function now that the bile is draining), then restaging and resection. CA 19-9 is 486 U/mL, measured after the bilirubin came down so that it reflects the tumor. She was told plainly that the aim is cure, that surgery after chemotherapy offers the best chance, and that the cancer can still return. [S]
Port placement next week; cycle 1 of modified FOLFIRINOX in two weeks.
Hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests drawn today; urine pregnancy test negative today.
Germline multigene panel sent after counseling; tumor molecular profiling on the EUS cores.
PCV20 and the first recombinant zoster vaccine given today, before chemotherapy.

Cancer-related pain (G89.3). Pain 6 out of 10 from the tumor, breaking her sleep. She wants a clear head for writing, so the plan starts low. [S]
Oxycodone 5 mg every 4 hours as needed, with senna.
Palliative care consultation in two days.
EUS-guided celiac plexus neurolysis if pain becomes severe.

Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency (K86.81). Pale, floating stools and weight loss from the blocked pancreatic duct; enzyme replacement is started on clinical grounds. [S]
Pancrelipase two capsules (72,000 lipase units) with meals and one with snacks.
Dietitian review this week.

Diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer (E08.9). Fasting glucose 141 mg/dL today confirms the A1c of 6.6% from the first visit. This is diabetes caused by the pancreatic disease, not type 2: weight loss and enzyme loss come with it, and insulin, not a drug that causes weight loss, is the treatment if one is needed. [S]
Home glucose meter and teaching.
No glucose-lowering drug yet.
Dexamethasone limited to day 1 of each cycle.
Dilated eye examination and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio to be arranged.

Iron deficiency anemia from blood loss (D50.0). Hemoglobin up from 9.1 to 10.4 g/dL after two doses of intravenous iron; no bleeding since. [S]
Continue pantoprazole.
Ferritin with the cycle 4 blood tests.

Epigastric pain with weight loss (R10.13). Explained by the diagnosis made today; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

New hyperglycemia (R73.09). Confirmed as diabetes due to the pancreatic cancer; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Pancreas-protocol CT of the abdomen with CT of the chest

At diagnosis, at each treatment phase, and when symptoms change
